topStories.headline: 80-Year-Old Killed by Tow Truck on Arguello Boulevard — While City's Funded Safety Project Sits Stalled
topStories.dek: Yuan Jun Zhu was struck in a crosswalk near Rossi Playground on Monday afternoon; advocates warn that more than $1.3 million in committed safety funding may be lost if SFMTA continues to delay.
topStories.body:
An 80-year-old man identified by Streetsblog San Francisco as Yuan Jun Zhu died Monday afternoon, September 28, after a tow-truck driver struck him in a crosswalk at the intersection of Arguello Boulevard and Anza Street in the Inner Richmond. The collision occurred steps from Rossi Pool and Playground, and the victim was transported to a hospital where he later died. According to SFPD public information officer Jennifer Gamble, the driver remained at the scene and is cooperating with investigators; no arrests had been made as of this writing.

WalkSF spokesperson Marta Lindsey said police told her the truck driver struck the pedestrian in a crosswalk while turning from Arguello onto Anza. The death was the city's 13th pedestrian fatality of 2026, according to the city's traffic-fatality tracker. Mayor Daniel Lurie issued a statement saying he was "deeply saddened" and that "street safety is public safety."

The crash has reignited pressure on city officials over a long-stalled safety project for Arguello Boulevard. SFMTA lists the Arguello Safety Project's status as "Planning" — more than three years after it was first promised. The stretch of Arguello north of Geary Boulevard remains on the city's High Injury Network. Despite Supervisor Connie Chan and former Supervisor Catherine Stefani directing $50,000 each in community funds toward the project, and former Assemblymember Phil Ting securing $1.25 million in state construction funds, no protected bike lanes or intersection redesigns have been built.

"We've been calling for improvements on Arguello for years, and the clock is running out to take action — funding for the project will be lost if it's not used soon," said Christopher White, executive director of the San Francisco Bicycle Coalition, in a statement reported by Streetsblog. SFMTA told Streetsblog this week that it is "currently developing designs for protected bicycle corners at multiple intersections along Arguello" and expects to vet them through interagency review in the next two months before a public hearing. Advocates noted that the agency has made similar promises before without follow-through.

topStories.headline: Kitchen Commons Set to Open This Fall in the Former Spanish Table Space on Clement Street
topStories.dek: Two Inner Richmond residents — one a co-owner of Liholiho Yacht Club — are turning a much-mourned retail vacancy into a neighborhood cookware shop with a café and cooking classes.
topStories.body:
Jeff Hanak, a partner at Liholiho Yacht Club, Good Good Culture Club, and Nopalito, and Connor Bruce, a former Nopalito chef, plan to open Kitchen Commons this fall at 130 Clement St., in the space vacated by the Spanish Table, which closed late last year amid eviction proceedings. The store will be stocked with new and vintage cookware — cast iron pans, local ceramics, knives, specialty pantry items, and cookbooks — and will include a small café serving coffee and prepared foods.

The owners also plan to host cooking classes, talks, and events such as cookbook exchanges. Both Hanak and Bruce are Richmond District residents who frequented the Spanish Table and did not want to see the Clement Street space go dark. "Given the mix of businesses on Clement Street, I thought this was a good opportunity to explore a business based on hospitality and craft," Hanak told the SF Standard when the project was announced in May.

Kitchen Commons is the latest in a wave of new openings on the corridor. According to a tally by blogger Kevin Wong, eight new food-and-drink concepts have opened or are slated to open on Clement Street within a twelve-month span, including Rose Pizzeria at 1 Clement St., which has drawn lines since its April opening, and Kissaten Hi-Fi, a Japanese matcha and Filipino-inspired coffee bar that opened in March at 189 Sixth Ave. Not everyone is enthusiastic: Mission Local has noted that some of the churn has displaced smaller independent businesses, including K-Elements BBQ, which closed after a landlord-driven rent increase.

events.title: Oktoberfest in the Presidio — Thursdays in October

events.description: The District 1 Family Summit invites families, caregivers, young people, and community members from the Richmond and surrounding neighborhoods to share their stories and help shape city priorities. Free to attend.

events.description: A free community public event combining Día de los Muertos and Diwali traditions at Presidio Tunnel Tops, open to all ages. No road closures are planned.

moreNews.headline: Sea Cliff Deed-Fraud Case: Permanent Injunction Hearing Set for October 23
moreNews.body: The Sea Cliff deed-fraud case covered in last week's issue moves to its next stage later this month. A temporary restraining order issued September 17 by San Francisco Superior Court Judge Charles F. Haines bars Brandon Aadee and Diana Peng from selling, encumbering, transferring, or otherwise affecting title to the property at 250 32nd Ave. while the city attorney's lawsuit proceeds. The city is seeking to void all eight disputed deeds and collect civil penalties of up to $2,500 per violation. A hearing on a permanent injunction is scheduled for October 23. Neither Aadee nor Peng appeared at the September 17 hearing; a San Mateo County arrest warrant is outstanding for Aadee.

moreNews.headline: New Outpost Meadow Picnic Pods at Presidio Now Reservable
moreNews.body: Starting October 1, the Presidio Trust opened reservations for picnic pods at the new Outpost Meadow, available at recreation.gov on a two-month rolling basis. Two pods — each with five to seven picnic tables, including accessible options — can be booked to guarantee space for large gatherings. One pod includes two double BBQ grills and shaded umbrellas. The meadow sits beside the Outpost playground near Presidio Tunnel Tops.

moreNews.headline: Two Storefronts at Sixth Avenue and Clement Street Appear to Be Closing
moreNews.body: Mission Local's Richmond Buzz column, published October 1, noted that two storefronts behind scaffolding at the southeast corner of Sixth Avenue and Clement Street appear to be closing. No replacement tenants have been publicly announced. Aroma Tea Shop at 302 Sixth Ave., between the two vacant spaces, appears to be remaining open.

restaurants.name: Burma Superstar
restaurants.description: The original 1992 Inner Richmond location that popularized Burmese cuisine in San Francisco, famous for its tea leaf salad and perpetual lines.

restaurants.name: Mandalay Restaurant

restaurants.name: Dalida

restaurants.name: Kitchen Istanbul
restaurants.description: A beloved Inner Richmond Turkish restaurant celebrated by sommeliers for its impeccable natural wine list and Eastern Mediterranean cooking.

restaurants.name: Lokma

restaurants.name: Aziza

restaurants.name: Bella Trattoria
restaurants.description: Long-running Inner Richmond Italian restaurant specializing in cucina napolitana, with housemade pastas and a loyal neighborhood following since 1996.

restaurants.name: Fiorella
restaurants.description: Neighborhood Italian wine bar and pizzeria known for blistered wood-fired pies and a lively Outer Richmond dining room.

restaurants.name: Rose Pizzeria
restaurants.description: Berkeley's nationally acclaimed pizzeria opened its first San Francisco outpost at the east end of Clement Street in April 2026, serving Neapolitan and Roman-style pies daily.

restaurants.name: Pizzetta 211
restaurants.description: Small, much-loved Outer Richmond pizzeria serving a short rotating menu of thin-crust seasonal pies in an intimate space with outdoor parklet seating.

restaurants.name: B Star
restaurants.description: Burma Superstar's sister restaurant offering a more eclectic, fusion-forward Burmese menu in a slightly more relaxed setting on Clement Street.

restaurants.name: Mamahuhu
restaurants.description: Bright and popular Clement Street spot serving approachable, flavor-forward Chinese-American dishes including mapo tofu and mala cucumbers.

restaurants.name: Hokkaido Sashimi Marketplace
restaurants.description: Inner Richmond counter serving fresh sashimi and to-go sushi rolls, a popular stop before a picnic in Golden Gate Park.

restaurants.name: Hard Knox Cafe
restaurants.description: Casual Outer Richmond diner serving Southern staples—fried chicken, cornbread muffins, and daily brunch until 3 p.m.—at honest prices.

restaurants.name: Kissaten Hi-Fi
restaurants.description: New Inner Richmond café rooted in the Japanese kissaten tradition, serving single-cultivar matcha and Filipino-inspired coffee in a slow, intentional setting.

hotels.name: Inn at the Presidio
hotels.description: The first hotel to open inside the Presidio national park site, housed in a beautifully restored 1903 Georgian Revival building with bay-view suites, complimentary breakfast, and evening wine receptions.

hotels.name: Lodge at the Presidio
hotels.description: Historic barracks building converted into a contemporary 42-room hotel on the Presidio's Main Post, offering free breakfast, forest and bay views, and a shuttle downtown.

hotels.name: Geary Parkway Motel
hotels.description: Renovated 20-room motel on Geary Boulevard offering free to-go breakfast and on-site parking within walking distance of Golden Gate Park.

shops.name: Green Apple Books
shops.description: Iconic Richmond District bookstore founded in 1967, stocking new and used titles across 8,000 square feet at the corner of Clement and Sixth Avenue.

shops.name: Park Life
shops.description: Inner Richmond design store and rotating gallery selling art books, locally made goods, prints, apparel, and limited-edition artist collaborations.

shops.name: Foggy Notion
shops.description: Inviting Clement Street boutique selling handcrafted ceramics, stationery, and locally made gifts with a warm, artisan-focused curation.

shops.name: Gaslight & Shadows Antiques
shops.description: Outer Richmond antique shop on Clement Street with a passionately curated selection of vintage objects and collectibles.

shops.name: Nijiya Market
shops.description: Well-stocked Japanese supermarket carrying fresh sushi-grade fish, Japanese pantry staples, and prepared foods popular with the neighborhood's Japanese community.

shops.name: New May Wah Supermarket

shops.name: Jane Consignment
shops.description: Outer Richmond consignment shop on Clement Street carrying quality pre-owned women's clothing and accessories.

shops.name: Love Street Vintage
shops.description: Curated vintage clothing boutique on Clement Street carrying a wide selection of women's vintage apparel and accessories.

artEntertainment.name: Legion of Honor
artEntertainment.description: Beaux-Arts museum in Lincoln Park founded in 1924, housing 6,000 years of European art, over 70 Rodin sculptures, and one of the largest prints-and-drawings collections in the country.

artEntertainment.name: Park Life Gallery
artEntertainment.type: Contemporary art gallery and design store
artEntertainment.description: Inner Richmond gallery space behind the Park Life store mounting rotating exhibitions of local and national artists, with about ten shows per year.

artEntertainment.name: Avenue 12 Gallery
artEntertainment.description: Small Inner Richmond gallery active in the Bay Area arts community, exhibiting local artists and Bay Area subject matter.

artEntertainment.name: Andy Goldsworthy Sculpture Trail
artEntertainment.description: Four permanent works by British sculptor Andy Goldsworthy installed across the Presidio—Wood Line, Spire, Earth Wall, and Tree Fall—all freely accessible on foot.

artEntertainment.name: Presidio Officers' Club
artEntertainment.description: One of the oldest buildings in San Francisco, the adobe-walled Officers' Club on the Presidio's Main Post houses free museum galleries exploring the site's 250-year history.

gymsRecreation.name: Richmond District YMCA
gymsRecreation.description: Full-service YMCA branch in the Inner Richmond offering cardio equipment, weight rooms, yoga classes, and youth programs for the neighborhood.

gymsRecreation.name: Presidio Community YMCA
gymsRecreation.description: YMCA branch inside the Presidio offering fitness classes, youth programs, and access to the Letterman Aquatics Center pool.

gymsRecreation.name: Folk Yoga Richmond
gymsRecreation.description: Intimate yoga studio at 182 Sixth Avenue offering vinyasa flow, power flow, prenatal yoga, and $15 community classes as part of San Francisco's largest locally owned yoga network.

gymsRecreation.name: Hot Yoga Plus
gymsRecreation.description: Outer Richmond studio on Geary Boulevard specializing in Bikram 26&2 yoga and Inferno Hot Pilates in a heated environment.

gymsRecreation.name: The Yoga Shala SF – Balboa Street
gymsRecreation.description: Richmond-area heated vinyasa yoga studio on Balboa Street, created for practitioners to thrive through consistent, community-oriented practice.

gymsRecreation.name: F45 Training
gymsRecreation.description: Franchise functional fitness studio on Geary Boulevard offering fast-paced group circuit workouts with attentive form coaching.

gymsRecreation.name: Live Fit Gym – Inner Richmond
gymsRecreation.description: Community gym at Arguello Boulevard offering strength training, power flow yoga, and fitness classes led by instructors including a licensed doctor of physical therapy.

gymsRecreation.description: Consistently ranked among the nation's top public courses, this 18-hole championship layout winds through eucalyptus and Monterey pine in the Presidio national park.

gymsRecreation.name: Golden Gate Park
gymsRecreation.description: More than 1,000 acres of meadows, trails, sports courts, and cultural institutions bordering the Richmond neighborhoods, used daily for running, cycling, tennis, and lawn sports.
